newsitem.title: UK: Scottish Power, utility shares gain.
newsitem.headline: Scottish Power, utility shares gain.

text.p: Shares in Scottish Power Plc and other UK utility companies rose on Tuesday, lifted by positive press comment in the wake of a review of regulation announced by the government on Monday, dealers said.
Scottish Power was up 14p at 404-1/2 by 0843 GMT and other electricity shares also rose, with PowerGen Plc up 6p at 721, National Power Plc 7p higher at 529 and Scottish Hydro Plc up 6p to 422-1/2.

Among water stocks, Wessex Water Plc was up 19-1/2p at 420, Anglian Water Plc rose 8-1/2p to 660, Thames Water Plc gained 6-1/2p to 700, Yorkshire Water Plc was up 9-1/2p at 400 and United Utilities Plc rose 19p to 679-1/2. South West Water Plc was up 13-1/2p at 718-1/2.
Analysts at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson were said to have made positive comment on selected utility stocks but analysts at the investment bank declined comment.

The Financial Times Lex column said there were signs of a "striking" change of rhetoric from Labour trade and industry minister Margaret Beckett in her announcement on Monday of a review of utility regulation.
It said Beckett appeared to be taking a less populist line against the profits made by utilities and that she appeared set on creating a long-term stable framework for the companies.
Once the expected windfall tax in Wednesday's budget, "utilities can look forward to less risk, a lower cost of capital and maybe higher valuations," the paper said.
